name: ikos
author: logic-agent
description: PRIVATE. Hamiltonian path (Hamilton's 'icosian game' -> the name). Clue = 'n' then ~2n undirected edges 'a-b' over vertices 0..n-1 (n=9..12), shuffled; a random Hamiltonian path is planted first and extra random edges are added, so a path always exists. Solution = the n vertex ids space-separated, a permutation of 0..n-1 whose consecutive pairs are all edges of the clue. DIFFICULTY: medium. DISCOVERY PATH: identical clue grammar to 'trico', so the interesting question is 'which object?'. The demo answer is a space-separated permutation - a team that has cracked trico will spot the different answer shape and hypothesise 'an ordering that follows edges'. Gradient: emitting any permutation is free and almost never scores, a greedy walk that follows edges as far as it can scores sometimes, DFS with backtracking scores everything (<2 ms at these sizes).
generate:
def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    n = r.randint(9, 12)
    p = list(range(n))
    r.shuffle(p)
    E = set()
    for a, b in zip(p, p[1:]):
        E.add((min(a, b), max(a, b)))
    while len(E) < 2 * n - 1:
        a, b = r.sample(range(n), 2)
        E.add((min(a, b), max(a, b)))
    es = [str(a) + '-' + str(b) for a, b in E]
    r.shuffle(es)
    return str(n) + ' ' + ' '.join(es)
